## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag does not read a default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, which the project's CLI-flag policy requires for every new flag, so CI cannot set exclusions through the environment. The skip logic in `collect` and the `--exclude` behaviour documented in `docs/flags.md` match each other, and the added tests cover them.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` now leaves out any file whose basename matches one of the patterns, and logs each skip. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect`, and end-to-end archive tests, plus a text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs `archive src`, nothing is excluded, because `--exclude` uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. Project policy `.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable … because CI sets options through the environment." — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment will quietly archive files they meant to skip. — Fix: Seed the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")` (decide and document how one variable holds several patterns, for example by splitting on a separator), and add an env-var case next to `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
